summary: For ceph/ceph, do not improvise an ad hoc Docker deployment when the official local paths are cephadm bootstrap or a full source-built vstart cluster; first verify root or passwordless sudo for cephadm, otherwise expect the fallback to require a heavyweight source build.
symptom: A host has Docker, systemd, ssh, and enough base runtime to look close to ready, but cephadm bootstrap cannot proceed and the repo-native fallback remains unstarted.
root_cause: Ceph's documented bootstrap path depends on host-level privilege and the repo-native alternative is a full source build with host dependency installation rather than a lightweight compose deployment.
fix: Check `sudo -n true` before spending time on Ceph bootstrap preparation.
If passwordless sudo is unavailable, stop before inventing a non-documented container topology and classify the host as unsuitable for the official cephadm path.
Treat the source-built vstart path as a separate heavyweight branch that needs source checkout, dependency installation, and long build time.
precheck: Verify whether the current user has passwordless sudo before attempting cephadm bootstrap.
Inspect proxy settings before assuming a large Ceph source checkout will complete quickly.
Budget for a full Ceph build only when host package installation privileges are available.
anti_pattern: Do not substitute an ad hoc single-container or compose-based Ceph layout for the official deployment just because Docker access exists.
Do not treat `systemd` plus Docker as sufficient proof that cephadm can run when sudo is still interactive-only.
quick_checks: Confirm whether the intended path is cephadm bootstrap or a full source-built vstart cluster before fetching large source trees.
If `http_proxy` or `https_proxy` is set, avoid assuming a Ceph repo clone will finish within the normal deployment budget.

summary: Repository-snapshot Keycloak builds can false-fail on transient Maven Central TLS handshake errors during large first-time dependency resolution, so treat one-off plugin-resolution failures as network noise first, not immediate project breakage.
symptom: Maven failed in keycloak-common while resolving maven-resources-plugin dependencies because a Central TLS handshake terminated mid-fetch.
root_cause: The first cold dependency bootstrap traverses a very large Maven graph, making transient remote handshake interruptions more likely than a real Keycloak build defect.
fix: Validate the missing artifact with direct curl to Maven Central before classifying the build as broken.
Preload the missing artifact into local cache or retry with a constrained TLS setting if the deployment truly requires source build.
precheck: Expect cold Keycloak repository builds to download a heavy Maven/Quarkus graph before any useful compile signal appears.
anti_pattern: Do not immediately treat a single Maven plugin handshake failure during a cold Keycloak build as proof that the repository build instructions are wrong.
quick_checks: If runtime deployment can follow the official stable image/distribution path, do not let a transient repository snapshot build handshake failure block business-app delivery.

summary: A local rebuild of `Piwigo/piwigo-docker` can false-fail on a transient Docker Hub auth-token EOF while pulling `library/alpine:latest`; when the official prebuilt `piwigo/piwigo:latest` image path is available, prefer it instead of spending retries on the cold rebuild.
symptom: `docker compose up --build` stalls at 0B on the Alpine base layer and then `docker pull alpine:latest` fails with `failed to fetch oauth token ... EOF`.
root_cause: The local rebuild path depends on a fresh Docker Hub token fetch for `library/alpine:latest`, which can transiently fail even though the prebuilt Piwigo image is otherwise retrievable.
successful_path: Record the local-build failure, switch back to the official prebuilt image path from the same upstream Docker workflow, and continue verification on the validated runtime rather than redesigning the stack.
fix: Test `docker pull alpine:latest` separately when a local rebuild stalls without layer progress.
If the official prebuilt image is available, use it rather than burning retries on the transient base-image fetch.
precheck: Differentiate a healthy slow pull from a zero-byte stalled base layer before changing the deployment shape.
anti_pattern: Do not keep retrying a cold local rebuild when the official prebuilt app image is already the documented deployment path and the failure is a registry token EOF.

summary: For osTicket on php:8.4-apache, gate the build on gd, intl, mbstring, mysqli, pdo_mysql, xml, and zip, and prefer the bookworm variant when the newer base image breaks extension setup.
symptom: Container builds can fail or produce a runtime-missing-extension deployment when osTicket dependencies are inferred loosely.
root_cause: osTicket requires a stable PHP extension set, and the newer distro image path made imap setup unavailable while additional headers such as libonig-dev and libxml2-dev were required.
successful_path: Use php:8.4-apache-bookworm, install the graphics and text dev packages plus libonig-dev and libxml2-dev, build the required extensions, and treat missing gd, intl, mbstring, mysqli, pdo_mysql, xml, or zip as a hard failure. Document imap and APCu as recommended-only when omitted.
fix: Pin to php:8.4-apache-bookworm instead of the newer base image when extension setup regresses.
Install libonig-dev and libxml2-dev before building mbstring and xml.
Audit the running container with php -m before classifying the deployment as valid.
precheck: List the required runtime extensions before the first image build.
Fail fast if the build path cannot provide the required extension set.
anti_pattern: Do not treat recommended-only extensions such as imap as hard blockers when the validated baseline flow does not require them.
Do not proceed to UI verification before the required PHP extension gate passes.
quick_checks: docker compose exec -T app php -m | rg -qx 'gd|intl|mbstring|mysqli|pdo_mysql|xml|zip'
Review build logs for missing libonig-dev or libxml2-dev when mbstring or xml fail to compile.

summary: For BigBlueButton 3.0, gate the run before deployment unless the host matches the official path: clean dedicated Ubuntu 22.04, root access, en_US.UTF-8 locale, sufficient RAM, and a real hostname for HTTPS/WebRTC.
symptom: The repository looks deployable, but the official self-hosting flow cannot even start cleanly on a generic workstation or VM host.
root_cause: BigBlueButton 3.0's official path is a host-native Jammy installation via bbb-install.sh with strict pre-install requirements; substituting an ad hoc container deployment would diverge from upstream.
successful_path: Before any install attempt, verify Ubuntu 22.04, passwordless root access, LANG=en_US.UTF-8, at least 16 GiB RAM for production, ports 80/443 availability, and a usable hostname for HTTPS. If these fail, stop early and classify as host-unsuitable rather than improvising Docker Compose.
fix: Run host-suitability checks before fetching or executing the installer.
Stop early when sudo is interactive-only or the OS is not Ubuntu 22.04.
Treat missing hostname/HTTPS prerequisites as a hard blocker for browser-usable delivery.
precheck: Run `sudo -n true` before any BigBlueButton install preparation.
Check `/etc/os-release` for Ubuntu 22.04 / jammy.
Check `cat /etc/default/locale` for `LANG=en_US.UTF-8`.
Check `free -h` and require at least 16 GiB RAM for production.
Check `hostname -f` and confirm a real DNS hostname is available for HTTPS.
anti_pattern: Do not invent a repo-local Docker Compose deployment when the official path is host-native via bbb-install.sh.
Do not classify the task as a normal app remediation problem when the host misses the installer's base prerequisites.

summary: For LibreOffice/core, verify host suitability before any large checkout: the official paths are a heavyweight Linux build or an even heavier WASM cross-build.
symptom: The target looks like a repository deployment candidate, but the official paths are multi-GB source builds with substantial host prerequisites and no lightweight service deployment.
root_cause: LibreOffice/core is the upstream office-suite source tree. Its official Linux flow needs package installation privileges, Java 17, and at least roughly 8 GB RAM, while the optional WASM flow needs an even heavier Emscripten and Qt toolchain and may require 64 GB RAM for linking.
fix: Read the upstream build docs and repo README before cloning large source trees.
Gate the run on passwordless sudo or equivalent package-install capability, Java 17 availability, and host RAM suitability before checkout.
Classify the run failed early when the host cannot satisfy those official prerequisites without ad hoc deviation.
precheck: Check `sudo -n true` before attempting dependency installation.
Check `java -version` or JDK presence before starting the official Linux build flow.
Compare available RAM against the upstream Linux minimum guidance and the WASM path memory guidance before any multi-GB clone.
anti_pattern: Do not start a 4 GB source checkout for LibreOffice/core before confirming the host can execute the official build path.
Do not invent a custom containerized service deployment for LibreOffice/core when the upstream repo is a desktop/WASM source tree.
quick_checks: Verify whether the target is the desktop source tree or a lighter downstream deployment artifact.
Require noninteractive privilege for documented package installation on Linux builds.
Treat the WASM path as a separate heavyweight branch, not a fallback for a weak host.

summary: The upstream unoconv script is not a drop-in fit for Ubuntu 24.04 defaults: it expects a python shebang target and still imports distutils, so a naive Python 3.12 runtime fails before the listener can start.
symptom: Container startup fails first with '/usr/bin/env: python: No such file or directory' and then with 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named distutils'.
root_cause: The upstream script shebang assumes python is present and its runtime code still imports distutils, which is removed from Python 3.12-based environments.
fix: Add python-is-python3 if the image does not provide /usr/bin/python.
Prefer Ubuntu 22.04 with python3-distutils for this project until upstream removes the distutils dependency.
precheck: Run unoconv --version in the target runtime before spending time on listener or bundle logic.
If the base image is Ubuntu 24.04 or another Python 3.12 runtime, expect an immediate distutils failure unless patched.
anti_pattern: Do not assume current distro Python defaults are compatible just because libreoffice and python3-uno install successfully.
quick_checks: docker compose logs should not show '/usr/bin/env: python: No such file or directory'.
docker compose exec -T unoconv unoconv --version should not fail with ModuleNotFoundError: distutils.
evidence: Ubuntu 24.04 failed twice before runtime was moved to Ubuntu 22.04 with python3-distutils.
After the runtime change, unoconv --version and conversion both succeeded.

summary: For JetBrains/intellij-community, gate the run before any large checkout unless the host can satisfy the official desktop build path: GUI-capable IntelliJ IDEA, JBR 25, at least 8 GB RAM, and disk headroom beyond standard runner-class capacity.
symptom: The repository looks like a source target but the official flow is a local GUI IDE build, and runner-class hosts fail basic prerequisite checks before build starts.
root_cause: The upstream project is a desktop IDE source tree with heavy disk requirements and GUI-local tooling expectations, not a normal deployable web/service app.
fix: Read the upstream README before cloning the full repository.
Check RAM, free disk, Java/JBR availability, and whether a graphical session exists.
If the host is runner-class or headless, fail early instead of inventing a non-official containerized desktop runtime.

Verify free disk exceeds standard GitHub-runner-class limits if upstream says those runners are too small.
Require DISPLAY or another supported GUI path before classifying a desktop IDE as deployable.
anti_pattern: Do not shallow-clone and build a huge desktop IDE repository on a host that already fails the documented disk and GUI prerequisites.
Do not fabricate a VNC/noVNC runtime when the task requires the official deployment path.
evidence: JetBrains README says standard GitHub runners are too small to build intellij-community.
JetBrains README requires IntelliJ IDEA 2023.2+, JBR 25 without JCEF, and minimum 8 GB RAM.
Current host had 6.9 GiB free disk, 7.7 GiB RAM total, DISPLAY unset, and no Java installed.

summary: MinecraftForge 26.1.2 source builds should be gated before execution unless the host can provide both a Gradle-supported runtime JDK and the project JDK 25 toolchain, full git tag history for changelog generation, and materially more free RAM/disk than a runner-class machine.
symptom: Gradle 8.12.1 fails on JDK 25, shallow clones break :createChangelog at tag 64.0, and MCP decompile/compile fails on low-memory low-disk hosts.
root_cause: The upstream Forge build for 26.1.2 requires a JDK split between Gradle runtime and project toolchain, full repository tag history, and more memory/disk headroom than this host had available for MCP/Vineflower setup.
fix: Run Gradle with JDK 21 while keeping JDK 25 available as a local toolchain path.
Fetch full repository history and tags before invoking the build so :createChangelog can resolve tag 64.0.
Gate the run unless the host has substantial free RAM/swap headroom and significantly more free disk than about 2.5 GiB on /.
precheck: java runtime split: prepare JDK 21 for Gradle and JDK 25 for the Forge toolchain.
git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository and fetch --unshallow --tags if true.
free -h and df -h / before setupMCP or installerJar.
anti_pattern: Do not run the Forge 26.1.2 Gradle build directly on JDK 25 with Gradle 8.12.1.
Do not rely on a shallow clone for this build.
Do not treat a host with only roughly 1.7 GiB available RAM and roughly 2.5 GiB free disk as sufficient for MCP decompile.
quick_checks: `JAVA_HOME=<jdk21> ./gradlew --version` should succeed before the real build.
`git tag --list 64.0` should return the expected tag before :createChangelog runs.
Require materially more headroom than `free -h` showing about 1.7 GiB available and `df -h /` showing about 2.5 GiB free.
evidence: DP_LOGS/minecraftforge-26-1-2/errors.log showed 'Unsupported class file major version 69' when Gradle ran on JDK 25.
DP_LOGS/minecraftforge-26-1-2/errors.log showed ':createChangelog' failing until the shallow clone was unshallowed and tags were fetched.
DP_LOGS/minecraftforge-26-1-2/errors.log captured repeated 'OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space' from Vineflower during MCP decompile.

summary: For ISPConfig, stop before deployment when the runner lacks root or passwordless sudo, because the official path is a full-host bootstrap for web, mail, DNS, FTP, and database services rather than a normal app-only install.

Refuse unsupported container-only approximations when the official flow is a host-level bootstrap.
precheck: Read the official documentation page first and confirm whether the install target is a full server or a normal application stack.
Run `id -u`, `id -un`, and `sudo -n true` before starting ISPConfig deployment work.

quick_checks: Confirm the official docs still recommend the autoinstaller/Perfect Server path.

fix: Check for a supported VM or physical target before treating pfSense as deployable.
Fail early on Linux runners missing /dev/kvm, qemu, bhyve, or FreeBSD build tooling.

Read the pfSense development start page before planning runtime execution.

summary: When building Go CLIs like okteto/okteto from a detached release-tag checkout on a host without Go installed, use a Go builder container with a non-login shell and `-buildvcs=false`; otherwise you can lose `go` from PATH inside the container or hit VCS stamping failures before runtime verification even begins.
symptom: Primary deployment stalls before runtime setup because `go` is unavailable on the host, then repeated build retries fail inside the builder container or on detached-tag VCS stamping.
root_cause: The host lacks a native Go toolchain, login shells inside the build container can overwrite the image PATH, and Go defaults to VCS stamping that fails on detached tag checkouts.
fix: Build inside an official Go container mounted over the source tree.
Use `bash -c` or another non-login shell so `/usr/local/go/bin/go` remains on PATH.
Pass `-buildvcs=false` when building from a detached tag checkout.
precheck: Run `command -v go` before assuming a host-native Go build path.
If building in a container, verify `docker run --rm golang:<tag> which go` and prefer non-login shells for the actual build.
If the source is checked out at a detached tag, add `-buildvcs=false` to the build command up front.
anti_pattern: Do not keep retrying a host-native `go build` when `go` is missing.
Do not use `bash -lc` in the Go builder container without checking whether it resets PATH.
Do not ignore `error obtaining VCS status` on detached tag builds.
quick_checks: Use `go build -buildvcs=false ...` for detached-tag source builds.

summary: During the WSO2 API Manager Docker build, host proxy variables can break Ubuntu apt metadata fetches with 502s, so apt should run with proxy env removed while the later GitHub release zip download can still use the proxy.
symptom: apt-get update failed on archive.ubuntu.com noble-backports with 502 through the host proxy.
root_cause: The build inherited a proxy route that was unreliable for Ubuntu mirrors, even though the GitHub release download path was fine through the proxy.
successful_path: Unset http_proxy/https_proxy/ALL_PROXY for the apt-get update/install layer, then let wget/curl use the proxy for the GitHub product zip and JDK downloads.
fix: Wrap apt-get update/install in env -u http_proxy -u https_proxy -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY -u all_proxy.
Keep the GitHub download steps untouched so they can still use the proxy path.
precheck: Watch for 502s from archive.ubuntu.com before restarting the whole build.
Only change the apt layer if the mirror failure is reproducible.
anti_pattern: Do not assume all external downloads should bypass the proxy.
Do not rebuild the whole stack before isolating the failing network layer.
quick_checks: docker build output shows apt-get update completing without 502s.

summary: For Zimbra/zm-mailbox, do not treat the repository as a standalone deployable app; upstream documentation routes real installs through the full Zimbra Collaboration host installer, which requires a supported OS, working sudo/root, and a license.

Gate the task early on supported host OS, working sudo/root, and license availability before attempting the official installer.
Fail rather than inventing an unsupported Dockerized approximation when the official product install is blocked.
precheck: Read `zm-mailbox` and `zm-build` READMEs before cloning large source trees or building packages.
Run `sudo -n true` and `cat /etc/os-release` before choosing the Zimbra installer path.
Confirm a Zimbra license key or file is available when targeting 10.1.x installer flows.
anti_pattern: Assuming `zm-mailbox` can be deployed directly as a standalone web application.
Proceeding with host-level Zimbra installation on unsupported Ubuntu releases without sudo/root.
Substituting an ad hoc containerized demo for the official Zimbra install path.
quick_checks: `curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zimbra/zm-mailbox/master/README.md` should describe source, not a standalone installer.
`curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zimbra/zinstaller/master/supported-os-installer.sh | rg check_sudoer` should confirm the privilege gate.

Inspect `src/middlewared/debian/control` for `truenas-*` package dependencies and `src/middlewared/middlewared/etc_files/local/nginx/nginx.conf.mako` for `/ui/` web UI expectations.

summary: For Garden local-kubernetes deployments on this host, validate local Kubernetes control-plane viability before spending time on project-level remediation: both kind and minikube can fail during bootstrap with in-container systemd errors when fs.inotify.max_user_instances is too low and no passwordless sudo is available to raise it.

root_cause: The host-level inotify instance ceiling is too low for the containerized control-plane init path, and the run has no passwordless sudo to change that prerequisite.
fix: Check /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances before committing to Garden local-kubernetes deployment on this host.
If the value is low and sudo is unavailable, do not spend retries on project config changes; move to a host with a working supported local Kubernetes runtime or elevate the host limit first.

sudo -n true

summary: For opnsense/core, do not treat a generic Linux Docker host as sufficient for a valid official deployment unless it can either build on stock FreeBSD as root or run the official appliance image with real externally publishable VM networking.

If forced to use Docker-hosted QEMU, do not classify the task as deployable until the actual browser UI is reachable from the host, not only the serial console and internal lighttpd listeners.
